public_product_rules: Low maintenance is a product requirement: no continuous pantry database is required to get value.
The shortest useful loop is choose -> optionally add accompaniments -> get/use one suggestion; buying is adjacent, not a prerequisite form.
One flexible primary selection model is preferred over duplicating the same decision into rigid meal-time forms.
Shopping uses simple local toggles/categories and stays separate from inventory truth.
Nutrient/balance bars stay compact and comparative; they must not dominate the screen or claim medical precision.
Mobile touch is primary; desktop click/drag remains supported; every visible control must actually respond.
No persistent bottom navigation/panel is required for the core experience.
Two-color active palette; visual depth is reserved for manipulable controls rather than page/card decoration.
Avoid large titles, explanatory paragraphs, arrow-dependent UI and circular-button inflation.
Responsive QA fails on overlap, unreachable controls, clipped tactile shadows, fixed lower panels or bars that crowd out the decision surface.
Public artifacts describe behavior and generic demo data only; personal foods, history, preferences and health context remain private/local.
negative_knowledge: Do not rebuild this as an inventory tracker.
Do not use a dashboard of nutrition KPIs as the home screen.
Do not add a bottom tab bar just because the page is mobile.
Do not split one decision into duplicate lunch/dinner forms without a new explicit reason.
Do not persist graph/balance projections as a second personal truth unless a future owner defines that schema.
Do not publish personalized food lists or consumption data into public Git recovery metadata.
Do not claim the reconstructed R08 candidate is the historical V12.2 or later accepted demo.
Do not infer authority from remembered filenames or version numbers.

privacy.method: Only generic product behavior and non-personal demo data are retained.
